title: Polynomial-Time Exact Learning of Fourier-Sparse Boolean Functions from Nearly Linear Quantum Samples
description: Research manuscript with PDF, LaTeX and internal review records. An algorithm exactly recovers every k-Fourier-sparse Boolean function with success at least 2/3 using O(k log^3(2k)) independent supplied uniform quantum examples and fixed-polynomial total computation and live space. Fresh residual estimates construct a queryable sign-majority hypothesis; known-function Fourier search and original-target certification contract missing Fourier energy. The theorem uses no target membership query or state-preparation inverse. All samples, adaptive refits and exact rational bit costs are charged. This complements Ye's smaller sample bound with a polynomial computational guarantee. No optimal logarithmic factor, practical implementation, noise robustness, exhaustive novelty, independent peer review, formal certification or BPP/BQP result is claimed. OpenAI Codex assisted derivation, source comparison, drafting and internal checking.
